rows.name: OpenID Connect Core 1.0: application-specific identity tokens and reauthentication
rows.reason: Client-specific ID-token audiences and freshness checks address cross-service credential misuse. ID tokens, access tokens and browser sessions differ; provider and every relying party must enforce checks.

rows.name: OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0
rows.reason: Provider-to-application logout notifications can terminate relying-party sessions. Each relying party needs session-termination implementation and a reachable endpoint; this does not automatically revoke every access token.

rows.name: AutoHotkey
rows.reason: Windows hotkey and macro automation does not provide identity federation, token audience enforcement, MFA policy, or session revocation for the service-security comparison.

rows.name: Authentik Authenticator Validation stage
rows.reason: Configurable MFA preserves second factors and limits recent-verification reuse. Login-stage configuration does not prove checks rerun for every app access; separately verify provider flows, recovery and application sessions.

rows.name: Authentik
rows.reason: Its OIDC providers, configurable MFA flows, and session controls directly support comparing token isolation and shared identity-provider compromise against separate password-and-2FA logins.

rows.name: RFC 9449 Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP)
rows.reason: Key-bound OAuth tokens resist theft-only replay when attackers lack proof keys. Requires client/authorization/resource-server support; Authentik support unestablished. Unrelated browser cookies remain outside scope.

rows.name: WebAuthn Level 2 public-key authentication
rows.reason: Origin-scoped public-key authentication strengthens provider/application login but does not remove stolen-session risk. Each application needs support; recovery and enrollment must preserve intended security.

rows.name: Authelia
rows.reason: Authelia documents OIDC and client two-factor policies. Switching providers does not remove concentrated-session risk. No mandatory exclusion; compatibility, enforcement and question-date version remain unverified.

rows.name: Independent per-service passwords plus 2FA
rows.reason: Independent passwords plus 2FA offer conditional compartmentalization while retaining session-theft risk. Credentials, recovery and administrative paths must be distinct; actual cross-service authentication, recovery and session behavior remain unspecified.

rows.name: Authelia
rows.reason: Its reverse-proxy and OIDC authentication modes provide a concrete SSO/MFA alternative; per-resource and per-client policies help compare authentication boundaries.

rows.name: Authentik
rows.reason: Relevant OIDC/MFA/provider flows, no mandatory exclusion. Relative security depends on unknown audiences, validation and session/reauthentication. Verify actual applications; isolation supports recommendation, validation/MFA bypass needs remediation.

rows.name: RFC 9700 OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
rows.reason: Audience/privilege restrictions, PKCE and refresh-token protection limit credential leakage and cross-service misuse when clients/servers implement them. PKCE does not prevent replay of already-stolen bearer tokens.

rows.name: Authentik User Login stage session controls
rows.reason: Lifetime/reuse controls bound the shared Authentik session. Ending it does not affect OAuth refresh tokens; browser persistence and independent application sessions require separate handling.

rows.name: Authentik OIDC SSO with separate application providers and enforced MFA
rows.reason: App-scoped tokens differ from central sessions. Version/client validation/MFA/audiences/refresh/session settings unknown; verify every integration's separate audiences and MFA/reauthentication. Verified enforcement supports deployment; failure needs changes or another approach.

rows.name: Authentik per-application authorization flow with fresh MFA for sensitive access
rows.reason: Require enrolled-factor validation in the provider authorization flow, without skip/recent-validation bypass; verify deployed-version boundary prompts. Mitigates SSO reuse, excluding existing downstream sessions and full Authentik compromise.

rows.name: AutoHotkey
rows.reason: Windows automation scripting does not supply the requested identity-provider/authentication-risk mechanism: operating-role mismatch. No Windows prohibition, impossibility of custom scripting, or failed must constraint is asserted.
